newsitem.title: INDIA: BA India flights cancelled due to strike.
newsitem.headline: BA India flights cancelled due to strike.

text.p: British Airways Plc said on Wednesday that all its India flights would be cancelled due to a 72-hour strike by the airlines' cabin crew.

"The strike has affected all flights to and from India. We are offering all passengers the option of their money back, a wait for our next available flight, or flights on other airlines," British Airways spokeswoman Rayana Sequiera told Reuters.
British Airways operates a daily flight out of Delhi and Bombay to London, two flights a week out of Calcutta and Madras to London, and five flights a week from Delhi to Dhaka.
A company statement said that nine flights out of India would be cancelled on July 11, 12 and 13, during the duration of the strike.
Sequiera said roughly 200 passengers per flight would be affected. Flights were not full, she said, as there was a lean patch with summer holidays in India over, and those in Europe just beginning.
She added that cargo would be affected by the strike too, as the airline carries it on its passenger flights. It carries about 250 tonnes of cargo out of India each week.
British Airways charges 24,400 rupees ($682) as economy class fare from Delhi to London.
